title: Scope Bootstrapping lets the Core Facilitator merge conflicting Atlas proposals that the Reconciliation Process reserves for voters
content:
A.1.15 establishes Scope Bootstrapping to resolve Governance Scope issues "swiftly" during the transition to the Endgame State, and A.1.15.1 is explicit about its force: "This Section defines bootstrapping measures that **can override requirements and specifications in the Atlas**. These bootstrapping measures are temporary."

A.1.15.1.1 then exercises that override: "When conflicting Atlas Edit Proposals are approved within a short period of each other, the Core Facilitator can decide to merge parts of the proposals together to ensure that the aggregate changes incorporate the best updates from each of the conflicting proposals."

This directly displaces the Reconciliation Process. A.1.11.2.5.2 and A.1.12.2.7.2 permit the Core Facilitator to consolidate only edits that are "non-conflicting / logically compatible," and state that where edits are "conflicting / logically incompatible... it falls to voters to decide which of the conflicting AEPs they wish to accept" via a Reconciliation Process Poll. A.1.15.1.1 hands that same conflicting case to the Facilitator, and the standard it applies — "the best updates from each" — is a substantive editorial judgment about merit, not a mechanical merge.

The tension is genuine and worth tracking. Under the standing process a Facilitator may never choose between incompatible amendments; under bootstrapping they may synthesize a text that no vote approved in that form. The justification is transition friction: a Reconciliation Poll costs another cycle, and during bootstrapping that delay is treated as the greater harm.

Two limits contain it. The measures are self-described as temporary, and the Facilitator remains bound by A.1.14.1.6.3-style alignment constraints and by the requirement in the Reconciliation Process that consolidation actions be publicly documented. But it remains the clearest case in this Article of speed being purchased with voter authority.
description: Temporary transition-era measures can override Atlas requirements; here the Facilitator may combine 'the best updates' from conflicting proposals rather than returning the choice to voters.
